$comment:
REQ-CBT-002: 'hybrid — externally understandable, internally multi-layered'. A player can read 'attack minus defence, x1.5 on a crit, give or take 10%' off this and be right. The layering is in what feeds attack and defence, not in the formula itself.

NOTE ON ELEMENTS: v1.0 §7 forbids substituting a fixed elemental rock-paper-scissors system, and §20 lists the element list and reaction matrix as needing approval. So elements are carried on skills and monsters but apply NO damage multiplier yet. `elementMultipliers` is deliberately absent rather than set to 1.0, so that adding it later is a visible decision rather than an edit to a number nobody notices.

damage.$comment: damage = (attack * skillPower - defence * defenceScale) * critMultiplier * variance, floored at minimumDamage.

accuracy.$comment: REQ-CBT-005. hitChance = base + (accuracy - evasion) * scale, clamped. A situational modifier is passed in by the caller.

critical.$comment: REQ-CBT-006. critChance is a percentage on the derived stat; critResistance is a boss-side reduction (REQ-CBT-010 keeps generic resistance a boss system).

resource.$note: Regeneration is deliberately slow relative to skill costs, so the burst/sustain axis in build identity has something to bite on.

threat.$comment: REQ-AI-003: threat from damage, healing and taunt; taunt adds significant threat; threat decays.
threat.$decayNote: 2% per second — enough that a tank must keep working, not so much that early threat is meaningless.

downed.$comment: REQ-CBT-012: at 0 HP a hunter is Downed, can be rescued, and dies if the timer expires.

movement.$comment: Combat is spatial along a single distance axis (see DL-025). Enough for range bands, closing, and formation; far short of a 2D navigation system the vertical slice does not need.

ai.$comment: How strongly build identity steers the utility layer. These are the numbers that make REQ-BLD-003 true or false, so they are the first thing to retune if builds start behaving alike.
ai.$reevaluateNote: AI decides far less often than physics ticks — required for 3-day offline catch-up to be affordable (risk R1).
